newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita sees clearly better 1997 op profit.
newsitem.headline: Merita sees clearly better 1997 op profit.

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy said on Wednesday it expected operating earnings to improve clearly this year.
"The Merita Group expects its operating result to improve clearly in the current year," Merita CEO Vesa Vainio said in a statement with the group's 1996 results.

"This projection is based on the continued likelihood of low interest rates, which will reduce the group's funding costs, and the steady, albeit decelerating, downward trend in non-performing receivables and other underperforming assets," Merita said.
"Other favourable developments include the decline in one-off integration expenses and the permanent cost benefits derived from the merger, the full impact of which is gradually being felt," it said.
Merita's banking arm Merita Bank's income-to-expenes ratio rose to 1.50 from 1.39.
Merita's operating profit after credit losses rose to 1.20 billion markka last year from 491 million in 1995.
"Merita's performance in the past year may be considered satisfactory," Vainio said, adding earnings had been in line with the group's own expectations.
Group operating profit came in slightly below the median of analysts' forecasts in a Reuters poll.
Merita proposed dividends of 0.20 markka per A share and 1.60 markka per B share, which, if approved by the annual general meeting, will be its first dividend payout to shareholders since 1991.
